bandReport.notes: All five assigned pages (p02, p04, p06, p08, p10) were opened and read from the column crops; itemsByPage was filled in page by page as I went. Item 1 opens my band cleanly and item 20 finishes at the foot of p10-c2, so nothing runs into a neighbouring band. DECIMAL SEPARATOR: this booklet uses the RAISED MIDDLE DOT (U+00B7), not a full stop - '1·6 billion', '7·2 billion', '9·6 billion', '10·9 billion' in the Passage-1 text and '1·2 : 1', '1·4 : 1', '1·6 : 1' in the options of item 13. Preserved as U+00B7 throughout, matching the shipped 2022-p2 / 2023-p2 / 2025-p2 convention. Curly quotes (U+2018/U+2019/U+201C/U+201D) and the em dash (U+2014) are likewise preserved as printed. COLUMN CROPS: all five pages split cleanly - the detected gutter sits at x=826 on every page and c1+c2 (838+883=1721) overlaps the 1653-px page width by 68 px, so no strip is lost between columns. Reading order was independently confirmed by two mid-sentence carries across a page boundary: Passage-3 breaks at 'in today's culture there' at the foot of p04-c2 and resumes 'seems to be a widespread presumption' at the top of p06-c1, and the RTE passage breaks at 'Teacher' at the foot of p08-c2 and resumes 'accountability systems and processes' at the top of p10-c1. Both were rejoined without inserting or dropping a word. BLOCK STRUCTURE: items 1-6 are standalone with no directions block. Items 7-10 sit under one 'Directions for the following 4 (four) items' block that contains FOUR separate passages, one governing each item - Passage-1 -> item 7, Passage-2 -> item 8, Passage-3 -> item 9, Passage-4 -> item 10 - so each item carries only its own passage, never the whole block. Items 11-13 share ONE bar graph. Items 14-16 share ONE set of figures. Items 17-20 share ONE two-paragraph passage. Following the shipped p2 convention (2019-p2 puts 18 of its 26 distinct passages against a single item), a reading passage goes in 'context' even where it governs only one item; the four shared contexts (11-13, 14-16, 17-20) were each composed once and pasted byte-identically. Every statement list and every 'Select the correct answer using the code given below' line is kept in the STEM, so no two items can collide on content_hash. FIGURES: four items depend on artwork that cannot be embedded here, and each is flagged 'figure-required' - item 1 (the polyhedron whose triangles are to be counted), item 5 (the velocity-time graph), items 11-13 (the steel-imports bar chart) and items 14-16 (the four rotated solids). For the last two I read the values off the printed artwork at 2x-7x magnification and tabulated them inside the figure description, so the items stay answerable without the image; the arithmetic and the spatial reasoning are untouched, no answer is implied. Bar-chart heights (thousands of tons): Jan 30/40/32, Feb 31/37/34, Mar 33/36/32, Apr 34/36/31, May 36/34/32, Jun 38/34/32 for Coil/Sheet/Scrap. Coil for April, May and June sits a fraction above the gridline (about 34.2, 36.2 and 38.3); I have recorded the nearest whole values and note the imprecision here. For items 14-16 each solid shows three faces and the dot counts were confirmed one solid at a time at 6x-7x: (I) top line, front 1 dot, right 2 dots; (II) top line, front 2 dots, right 3 dots; (III) top line, front 3 dots, right 4 dots; (IV) top cross, front 2 dots, right 1 dot. The stroke on the top face is drawn slanting in (I) and (III) and horizontal in (II); that orientation is recorded in the figure description as an observation only. SUSPECTED PRINT DEFECT, transcribed as printed and NOT corrected: the RTE passage shared by items 17-20 reads 'from regularly attending and complementing elementary education' where the sense wants 'completing'. Verified on the page image; 'complementing' is what is printed, so that is what is stored. NUMERALS: on p04 the phrase 'in 2050 and 10·9 billion in 2100' sets '2100' with a visible gap ('2 100') because that line is heavily justified; adjacent '2050' on the same line has no gap, so I read the gap as kerning rather than content and stored '2100'. LAYOUT NOT REPRESENTABLE: item 3 prints its four rows of numbers as a column-addition, with a short horizontal rule under each entry of the THIRD row separating the three operand rows from the result row. A GFM table cannot express a mid-table rule, so the grid is stored as a four-column table with an EMPTY header row, which keeps all four printed rows as body rows in their printed order rather than promoting the first row to a header it never was. The position of the rule is recorded here instead. No item number is missing or repeated in 1-20, every item has exactly four options, none is blank, no two options within an item are identical, and no answer field is supplied anywhere.

questions.context: Global population was around 1·6 billion in 1990—today it is around 7·2 billion and growing. Recent estimates on population growth predict a global population of 9·6 billion in 2050 and 10·9 billion in 2100. Unlike Europe and North America, where only three to four per cent of population is engaged in agriculture, around 47 per cent of India’s population is dependent upon agriculture. Even if India continues to do well in the service sector and the manufacturing sector picks up, it is expected that around 2030 when India overtakes China as the world’s most populous country, nearly 42 per cent of India’s population will still be predominantly dependent on agriculture.

options.label: B
options.text: Indian economy greatly depends on its agriculture.

options.label: C
options.text: India should take strict measures to control its rapid population growth.

questions.context: I am a scientist, privileged to be somebody who tries to understand nature using the tools of science. I find it oddly anachronistic that in today’s culture there seems to be a widespread presumption that scientific and spiritual views are incompatible.

questions.context:
It is no longer enough for us to talk about providing for universal access to education. Making available schooling facilities is an essential prerequisite, but is insufficient to ensure that all children attend school and participate in the learning process. The school may be there, but children may not attend or they may drop out after a few months. Through school and social mapping, we must address the entire gamut of social, economic, cultural and indeed linguistic and pedagogic issues, factors that prevent children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups, as also girls, from regularly attending and complementing elementary education. The focus must be on the poorest and most vulnerable since these groups are the most disempowered and at the greatest risk of violation or denial of their right to education.

The right to education goes beyond free and compulsory education to include quality education for all. Quality is an integral part of the right to education. If the education process lacks quality, children are being denied their right. The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act lays down that the curriculum should provide for learning through activities, exploration and discovery. This places an obligation on us to change our perception of children as passive receivers of knowledge, and to move beyond the convention of using textbooks as the basis of examinations. The teaching-learning process must become stress-free; and a massive programme for curricular reform should be initiated to provide for a child-friendly learning system, that is more relevant and empowering. Teacher accountability systems and processes must ensure that children are learning, and that their right to learn in a child-friendly environment is not violated. Testing and assessment systems must be reexamined and redesigned to ensure that these do not force children to struggle between school and tuition centres, and bypass childhood.
